pull first, it's been a minute

The reviewed result-obligation prerequisite is committed as `a983a2043`, and the classification check passes against that commit. The package check is still validating the packed workspace. After it finishes I’ll push this qualified chunk, then add the mixed-JDK discovery regression.

`origin/master` is still an ancestor of the schema commit, so there is no merge to resolve before publication. The package checker has already confirmed the v5 schema is in the facade archive and is now compiling the unpacked package set. I’m waiting for that result before pushing.

The same-version JDK fixture is now in the tree. It sets two source roots to different JDK homes with the same reported version and asks preparation to retain two distinct artifact digests. The package checker is still compiling its unpacked copy; I’ll run the fixture against the current discovery code to confirm it fails for the expected deduplication.

The red fixture is compiling while the package check continues in its unpacked copy. Both processes are active. I’m holding the source stable until the fixture confirms the specific discovery failure, then I’ll change only the version-based coalescing path.

The red fixture has reached the analysis test binary and is still compiling. The package check remains active without an error. Once the fixture runs, I’ll use its exact assertion failure to confirm the discovery fix addresses the missing second artifact.

The fixture failed at the intended assertion: discovery returned one dependency for two configured homes. I removed the version-only coalescing, retaining path deduplication and leaving exact byte identity to preparation. I’m rerunning the fixture to verify both artifact digests survive.

The fixed fixture is rebuilding. The package check has no error output but is still compiling from its isolated unpacked tree. I’m keeping these validation streams separate: the package run qualifies the schema commit, and the focused fixture qualifies the new JDK discovery change.

The remote remains at `3ed541ac0`, with no concurrent merge needed for `a983a2043`. I’m holding publication until the package checker returns because this change adds a shipped schema file. The fixed JDK fixture is also still compiling.

Both validations are still active: the JDK regression is rebuilding analysis, and the package checker is compiling an extension consumer from the packed crates. There is no failure output. I’m letting each finish because they cover separate risks introduced by this work.

The mixed-JDK fixture now passes: discovery and preparation retain both same-version homes with two distinct artifact digests. I’ll run the neighboring JDK discovery tests and lint this change, then checkpoint it separately. The schema package check is still compiling its consumer.

The neighboring JDK discovery selection passed all four tests. Clippy and the package set are still running. The remaining #3649 work is larger than this discovery fix: prepared packs currently keep a dependency ID and artifact digest, while per-file selection names a home. I’m tracing that identity bridge before changing resolver output.

Both long checks remain live and CPU-bound. The JDK behavior change itself has passed its red/green fixture and neighboring tests; I’m waiting for workspace lint before committing it, and for the package check before publishing the schema commit.

The package check passed: all 19 archives and unpacked consumers validated with the v5 schema included. I’m publishing the committed schema checkpoint now. The JDK discovery fix remains separate and will be committed after its lint gate.

The JDK discovery slice now passes its four neighboring tests and workspace Clippy. I’m checkpointing it as a separate change: it preserves both artifact candidates but does not yet bind either one to a Java call, so B4/B5 remain inactive.

Both qualified prerequisites are now on `origin/master`: schema `a983a2043` and same-version JDK discovery `f1d0dca5a`. I’m posting their precise scope on #3561 and #3649, then continuing the per-call artifact join. Neither commit enables B4/B5 findings.

The pull is done, and the two preparatory commits are on `origin/master`. I’m continuing with the missing link between a Java call and its selected JDK artifact, which B4 and B5 need before they can report findings safely.

I found a second identity loss after discovery: activation keeps only one matching JDK evidence row per model shard. I’m fixing that first and adding a regression for two distinct artifacts with the same release version. That preserves the evidence the later call binding must compare.
The activation regression is compiling. I also traced where the selected home can be published with the model snapshot, so a query can compare an exact prepared digest without reading the JDK again.

The new activation tests pass, including the case where a JDK 21-only model must exclude a JDK 22 artifact. I’m checking the workspace gate, then I’ll preserve a unique discovery-to-preparation correlation for JDK homes that report the same version.

The 186 semantic-model tests pass. I tightened activation so the manifest’s JDK version requirement is checked on each retained artifact row; the focused runtime tests are rerunning after that final change.

The final runtime rebuild is still compiling. The same-version regression remains the key check: a model may activate against both prepared artifacts, but a finding must later match the source file’s selected artifact exactly.

The focused runtime tests pass after the final change. The full workspace Clippy gate is still running; once it finishes I’ll publish this activation slice and continue the source-home-to-prepared-digest join.

Commit `2c2514ad6` is on `origin/master`, and I updated #3649 with its exact scope. I’m now connecting each configured JDK home to the prepared artifact digest; duplicate release versions need separate correlation IDs during that preparation pass.

The host-side map is now wired into the same immutable model publication as the activated shards. A missing or unprepared JDK home has no entry, so later call binding will remain incomplete. I’m compiling that path before adding the production-path fixture.

The production-path fixture is rebuilding with two configured JDK homes and one release version. I’ve confirmed the ordinary Java resolver sees both activated declaration packs as ambiguous today, so the next change will let that resolver use the source file’s exact prepared JDK selection when one exists.

The resolver now filters activated JDK declaration facts by the prepared artifact selected for that Java file. The mixed-home regression is compiling; it checks each module’s own method is bound and the method found only in the other home stays unresolved.

The first mixed-home call test reached the external boundary but did not produce a member proof. I’ve added temporary declaration details to the failing assertion so I can identify whether the selected pack lacks the method or the resolver loses it during lookup.
The pull is done. I’m continuing the Java Batch B work by checking the failing mixed JDK test, then I’ll fix the artifact selection and call proof it exposed.

The failing fixture shows a real identity gap: the active overlay merges equal named JDK types from two prepared artifacts, so a source file can lose its own type declaration before member lookup. I’m tracing the overlay’s record selection now; the fix needs to preserve artifact provenance without changing ordinary resolution.

I found a safe way to keep both JDK declarations: retain equal records when they came from different artifact digests, while preserving the existing deduplication for other packs. The mixed-home test now uses real zero-argument `String.trim()` and `String.strip()` methods, whose signatures I checked against the Java 21 API.

The resolver test is rebuilding with the artifact-aware overlay change. Once it passes, I’ll attach the selected declaration’s JDK provenance to the exact call proof; the source file’s JDK binding alone must not make a third-party call eligible for a JDK model.

The two-module test now passes: each module resolves only the method in its selected JDK artifact. I’ve also added a guard so a third-party call in the same source file carries no JDK applicability evidence. The three focused tests are rebuilding now; next I’ll run the broader native and repository gates before publishing this slice.

The 237 related native tests passed. I added missing and conflicting source bindings to the production fixture, and bumped the generated pack cache version because the reviewed `String` call shapes change generated pack meaning. I’m checking those new near misses now, then I’ll run Clippy and publish the validated chunk.

Clippy found one issue in the new activation path: adding the JDK map pushed a function over the repository’s argument limit. I’m grouping the two pieces of publication evidence into one value, then I’ll rerun the gate.

The new missing and conflicting binding cases pass. Origin/master has no concurrent changes at this point, and formatting and classification checks are green. Clippy is rerunning after the argument cleanup; when it finishes I’ll commit and push this #3649 slice, then continue with the model applicability join.

Clippy has passed the changed analysis crate and is checking downstream crates now. The mixed-home fixture also confirms that a module with no binding, or two conflicting bindings, does not receive an exact JDK call proof.

The artifact selection slice is now on origin/master as `41d448938`. Its focused and related native tests, formatting, workspace Clippy, and classification checks passed. I’m recording the evidence on #3649, then I’ll implement the remaining model-side artifact join before treating B4/B5 as eligible.

The call proof now carries the full selected JDK evidence row into the semantic target. I added a binder for reviewed JDK result-use obligations that requires exact row equality and an applicable call shape, plus a test for equal-version artifacts with different digests. I’m running that test before wiring any policy finding to it.

The binder test is still compiling. While reviewing its lookup path, I found another case to cover: two active JDK model shards can publish identical claims for different artifacts, and generic winner selection may collapse them before the artifact check. I’ll filter by the selected artifact before choosing a reviewed obligation.

The direct binder test passed. I’ve now added artifact filtering before model winner selection, so equal summaries from different JDK installations remain distinguishable. A second native case checks that behavior; after it passes I’ll verify the full resolver-to-semantic-target path.

The first model-selection test exposed a JVM keying mistake in my new lookup: the summary index uses the shared JVM realm key. I corrected the key and am rerunning the focused test. The failure was confined to the new filtered lookup; the already published call-artifact slice remains green.

The artifact-filtered model test passed after the key correction. I’m now exercising the full path through Java semantic materialization and dispatch, checking that each mixed-JDK module’s target retains its own complete activation evidence. That is the remaining native proof before I connect B4/B5 to a policy row.

The full dispatch fixture is still rebuilding the analysis test binary. The next implementation step is a typed RQL result-use row that joins the existing exact Java discard classification, the selected JDK artifact, and reviewed model obligations. I’m keeping `File.delete()` open until dispatch can prove every feasible receiver target.
I’ve pulled the current master. I’m checking the in-progress Java result-use work against it, then I’ll give you the next build target and the acceptance bar.

Fresh fetch confirms our HEAD and `origin/master` are identical. I’d build the Java B4/B5 result-use pipeline next: join an exact discarded-result fact to the call’s selected JDK artifact and a reviewed return obligation, then require every feasible dispatch arm to agree. `String.trim()` is the first B4 case. B5 needs a reviewed status API with precise failure semantics; I won’t treat `File.delete()` as proven while virtual dispatch is open. I’m finishing the artifact-binding gate before adding policy findings.

The artifact test now passes through production Java dispatch. It also confirms that a syntax-only target carries no JDK applicability proof. I’m checking the workspace build, then I’ll commit this prerequisite and wire the result-use relation into RQL.

The exact artifact binder is now on `origin/master` as `35138e59c`, and #3649 has a status update. The next implementation target remains one RQL row for reviewed, discarded results, with an explicit incomplete result whenever syntax, artifact selection, model binding, or dispatch coverage is uncertain.

Fresh fetch confirms the branch is current with `origin/master`. I also pushed the validated JDK artifact-binding work as `35138e59c`.

**Build next:** Java B4/B5’s typed RQL result-use relation. It should report an ignored result only when the exact Java syntax discards it, the call binds a reviewed obligation from its selected JDK artifact, and every feasible dispatch arm agrees. Start with `String.trim()` for B4; choose a B5 status API only after reviewing what its return value means.

#3649 and #3561 remain open. The relation, policies, CLI JSON/SARIF/MCP checks, and pinned corpus evidence still need qualification.

I’m continuing Java Batch B from the pushed artifact-binding change. I’ll inspect the current tree and the RQL result and policy paths, then implement the B4/B5 relation with explicit incomplete results for unresolved calls.

I found a model-selection edge case: an ordinary JDK summary can outrank a reviewed obligation for the same call. I’m making the obligation lookup filter records before ranking them. That lets B4/B5 use a narrow reviewed pack without changing unrelated flow summaries.

The new JDK 21 model is deliberately narrow: `String.trim()` has a pure-result obligation; `Files.deleteIfExists(Path)` has a status obligation whose `false` value means the path was absent, while I/O errors still throw. I’m validating the authored pack and adding a separate RQL row so policies can distinguish those obligations.

The authored JDK 21 pack now validates and compiles, and its embedded bytes match the reviewed source in a native test. I’ve wired the RQL vocabulary and row type and am compiling the execution path now. I’ll test positive, consumed-result, wrong-artifact, and incomplete cases before adding either policy.
I’ll check the local changes, fetch the latest origin/master, and merge it into the current branch before continuing Java Batch B.
origin/master is already current; the pull made no changes. The Java Batch B work is still uncommitted in this workspace, so I’m continuing from that state.

The RQL parser test passes. I’m adding an end-to-end Java fixture with a pinned JDK source archive so the rule proves it can bind a discarded call to the exact selected artifact, while keeping calls without that proof incomplete.

The test fixture now includes a JDK 21 source archive and activates the reviewed pack through the production dependency path. Compilation is still running; the test will tell us whether the full call-to-artifact join produces a positive row.

The discarded `String.trim()` case now passes through exact source selection and model activation; the assigned result stays a nonfinding. I’ve added `Files.deleteIfExists(Path)` to the same fixture to check the separate status-result path before wiring the two policies.

The first status test stayed incomplete because the generated JDK declaration did not certify the exact `deleteIfExists(Path)` overload. I added that reviewed owner, static method, and parameter signature to the JDK producer and rotated its generated-pack cache version. The fixture is rerunning now.
